name: Judas
overview: Judas, identified as Barsabbas, was a male leader among the early Christian brethren as noted in Acts 15:22. While his tribal affiliation and family details are not recorded, he held a significant role within the church community. No additional personal notes are provided beyond his leadership status.
namesAndTitles: The name Judas means 'praised,' while Barsabbas means 'son of seven,' both proper names mentioned in Acts 15:22. These names reflect common Hebrew naming traditions but were not given by God specifically in this context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Judas beyond his designation as Barsabbas and his leadership role among the brethren. No other relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Judas, called Barsabbas, is significant as a leading figure within the early church, demonstrating the growth and organization of the Christian community after Christ's ascension. His mention alongside other leaders highlights the importance of faithful service and guidance in the body of believers. Though not directly linked to the Messiah's lineage, his role supports the unfolding mission of Christ's followers.
